cap_confirmation: Resolved opponent levels equal cap+offset-2 at cap 36: Coalossal L35 (36+1-2), Torracat L38 (36+4-2), Fletchinder L39 (36+5-2), Numel L40 (36+6-2), Litleo L40 (36+6-2), Heatmor L35 (36+1-2). All six match, including the deliberately inflated unevolved members.
party_note: Same six as the rest of the cap-36 block, reordered Water-first for a six-member mono-Fire room. Excadrill was deliberately placed last because it is 2x weak to Fire.

attempts.notes: Mega Blastoise's Mega Launcher Water Pulse is 2x or 4x into all six members and did almost all the work. Lost Azumarill to a Tough Claws Thunder Punch and Mamoswine to a Choice Specs Overheat - both correct AI target choices.

strategy_checks.check: Coalossal uses Tar Shot to lower Speed and double the target's Fire weakness
strategy_checks.evidence: Coalossal chose Protect on turn 1 and Tar Shot on turn 2, but by then a 4x Water Pulse had already KOed it before its move resolved. Tar Shot never landed. The turn it was supposed to fire was turn 1, behind its partner's Fake Out.

strategy_checks.check: ALLY_COMBO: Torracat's Fake Out buys the turn for Coalossal's Tar Shot, then the team exploits the Fire vulnerability
strategy_checks.evidence: The Fake Out half fired correctly on turn 1 (flinched Azumarill), but Coalossal spent that protected turn on Protect instead of Tar Shot. The two halves of the authored two-step were on the same turn as each other and the wrong way round. See defect P10-D17.

strategy_checks.check: Torracat's Intimidate lowers the opposing Attack on entry
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 0 state already shows atk -1 on both Mega Blastoise and Azumarill before any decision.

strategy_checks.check: Numel's Simple doubles Stockpile into +4 Defence and +4 Special Defence
strategy_checks.evidence: Numel had three decision points (Protect, Protect, Protect - the third failed) and never selected Stockpile. Simple was inert for the whole battle and Numel died at full HP to one 4x Water Pulse. Its Eviolite and its +6 offset are both paying for a defensive setup role it never attempted.

strategy_checks.check: Litleo's Choice Specs locks it into one move
strategy_checks.evidence: Overheat on both of its turns. The first one KOed a full-HP 136 HP Mamoswine through Thick Fat, which is a genuinely frightening amount of damage from a L40 unevolved Pokemon and fully justifies the +6 offset.

The only contact move I aimed at a Flame Body holder was Azumarill's Liquidation into Coalossal on turn 2, which was redirected into Torracat's Protect. No contact ever landed on Coalossal or Fletchinder.

strategy_checks.check: Misty Terrain is active in the Lavaridge Gym (the dossier repeatedly reasons about it: 'Misty Terrain does not prevent Tar Shot, Intimidate, Stockpile or flinching')
strategy_checks.evidence: Terrain read 'none' for all eight turns of this battle. Both Cole's and Gerald's dossier blocks discuss Misty Terrain as an active field condition of the gym, but no terrain was present on the driven board. Either the gym field effect is not applied through this battle path, or the dossier prose describes an intent that the source does not implement. Flagging for book/source reconciliation rather than treating it as an AI defect.

protect_ledger.payoff: REAL for damage, COSTLY for the plan - it blocked a 4x Mega Launcher Water Pulse, but it is also the turn the authored Tar Shot was supposed to go out behind the partner's Fake Out.
REAL - Coalossal died to Water Pulse and Azumarill's Liquidation redirected onto Torracat, which Protected it away at 2x.
REAL - blocked both a 2x Focus Blast and a 4x Water Pulse on the turn it entered.
EMPTY - consecutive Protect, 'But it failed!', and it died to the Water Pulse it tried to block.

ai_defects.board: Coalossal L35 leading at full HP with Tar Shot available, while its partner Torracat selected Fake Out the same turn
ai_defects.why_wrong: This is the authored two-step and the AI had both halves in hand. Fake Out was going to flinch one of my two attackers regardless, so Coalossal's turn was already partly covered - that is precisely the window the dossier describes for Tar Shot. Protecting instead meant Tar Shot was pushed to turn 2, by which point Coalossal was dead. The two members are not coordinating: each scored its own defensive option in isolation.
ai_defects.better_action: Tar Shot on turn 1 on Mega Blastoise, which would have halved its Speed and doubled the Fire damage the other five members deal for the rest of the fight.

ai_defects.board: Numel L40 with Eviolite and Simple, at full 135 HP both turns
ai_defects.chosen: Protect, then Protect again ('But it failed!')
ai_defects.why_wrong: Numel carries Simple specifically so one Stockpile is worth +4 Defence and +4 Special Defence, which on an Eviolite body would have made it genuinely hard to remove. It never used it, and the second Protect was a guaranteed failure that killed it. This is the same class of defect as Thievul's Snarl, Cyclizar's Shed Tail and Alcremie's Decorate: the move that defines the set loses to an immediate defensive or damage option.
ai_defects.better_action: Stockpile on turn 6 behind its partner, then Protect or attack from +4/+4.

level_change_decision: KEEP. Won on attempt 1 with two faints in a six-member room. The offset spread is the most interesting in the block and it works: the three unevolved members carry +4 to +6 and Litleo at L40 with Choice Specs one-shot a full-HP Mamoswine, which is exactly the 'compensate the unevolved members individually' intent from the dossier paying off. Coalossal and Heatmor at +1 are correctly the ordinary bodies.
could_this_be_cooler: The level-compensation idea here is genuinely good and I would not change it - a L40 Choice Specs Litleo is a better encounter than a L36 Pyroar would be, and it reads as a gym trainer who has raised his baby Pokemon hard. The problem is that two of the six sets never do their thing: Tar Shot arrives a turn late and Stockpile never arrives at all, so what should be a layered room plays as six Fire-types taking turns. Suggestion, not applied: Coalossal's Protect competes directly with the Tar Shot the team is built around - if the support member simply did not have Protect, the two-step would be forced, and the same is true of Numel, whose Protect is the move beating Stockpile in scoring. Removing one defensive button from each of the two support members would probably fix both without touching a single stat.
authored_set_legality: No legality problems. Flame Body, Intimidate, Simple, Unnerve, Tough Claws, both Eviolites and the Choice Specs all behaved as printed.
notes: The Misty Terrain discrepancy above applies to Gerald (E0144) as well and is the one thing in this battle that needs a decision from the book side rather than the AI side.
